subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: The Second Sex and Feminist Awakening
description: Learn The Second Sex and Feminist Awakening in one minute.

hook.text: In 1949, Simone de Beauvoir published a book arguing that women were not born inferior but made that way.

buildup.text: The Second Sex examined how history, religion, and culture had systematically defined women as lesser.

discovery.text: Her famous line 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' became a foundational feminist idea.

twist.text: The Vatican placed the book on its list of forbidden texts, and critics called Beauvoir obscene.

climax.text: The book ignited second-wave feminism and remains one of the most influential works on gender ever written.

punchline.text: One sentence rewrote how the world understood gender.

quiz.question: What was Simone de Beauvoir's central argument in The Second Sex?
options: Women are naturally suited for domestic roles
Women are not born inferior but are made so by society
